summary: Toolchain serial negotiation is blocking streamed responses, causing p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Dedicated (example: FocusDocs) are seeing a sharp increase in streaming inference tail latency (p95/p99) and intermittent 504 timeouts for requests that trigger function/tool calls. The regression started after a canary of tool-proxy v2.3 was promoted to us-east on 2026-03-12.

Impact:
- Customer-facing streaming responses stall for up to 20s at the tail; p99 token latency increased from ~400ms to >6s.
- Some requests end with 504 Gateway Timeout when the tool-call negotiation takes too long, which causes downstream application errors.
- Affects customers with tool-enabled messages on Dedicated capacity; focus customer reported production errors.

Environment:
- Prod - us-east, Dedicated cluster dc-us-east-09
- Tool-proxy service v2.3 (canary then promoted), api-gateway v1.18, serving-runtime stable v3.6

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Send a streaming chat request that triggers a tool call (schema validation + tool metadata fetch).
2. Server starts streaming tokens, then stalls after the preflight negotiation step while awaiting tool metadata handshake.
3. If handshake exceeds timeout (configurable), client sees a 504 or streaming connection closes.

Observed behavior:
- Serial/locking behavior in the tool-proxy negotiation path appears to block the streaming event loop per-connection while performing a synchronous schema fetch and capability negotiation with external adapters.
- Metrics show a spike in tool-proxy synchronous RPC latency (p99 ~7s) and corresponding increase in streaming completion latency.

Expected behavior:
- Tool negotiation should be async/non-blocking for active streams; schema fetches should be cached or parallelized so they don't add head-of-line blocking to token emission.

Logs & traces:
- Example trace: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/0a9f2c (shows tool-proxy wait step 5.2s)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Alert: latency SLO page reported p99 token latency increase for dc-us-east-09; pager duty triggered.
Checked deployment history: tool-proxy v2.3 promoted to us-east at 2026-03-12 21:40 (canary successful) then full promotion 2026-03-12 23:05.
Correlated spikes with tool-proxy: api-gateway and serving-runtime CPU/latency unchanged; tool-proxy sync RPC p99 rose from 120ms -> 7s.
Heap/threads on tool-proxy instances show normal usage; root cause appears to be synchronous preflight 'schema verification' loop that retries on 408s and blocks the stream goroutine.
Captured example request IDs and traces: trace IDs: [0a9f2c, b3d44a, c1f002] (links in Confluence).
Hypothesis: v2.3 introduced a serial negotiation step to ensure schema freshness; missing cache TTL and retry backoff causes serialization under contention leading to head-of-line blocking.
Reproduced locally by running a tight loop of tool-enabled streams; when tool-proxy is rate-limited or external adapter slow, token emission stalls until handshake returns.
Related PRs: infra#7218 adjusted default tool-proxy rollout settings; tool-proxy#214 added schema-sync on connect.
comments: 2026-03-13 10:02 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer FocusDocs reported 504s for streaming calls that use tool validation. They escalated to enterprise SLA team. Details in support thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/support/streams-2026-03-13
2026-03-13 10:25 - Diego Ramirez (Oncall Eng): Noted correlation with tool-proxy v2.3 promotion. Kicked off deeper trace analysis; asking infra to temporarily divert traffic off v2.3 canary nodes.

2026-03-13 11:40 - SRE (Lauren Chen): Applied config change to disable 'sync_schema_fetch_on_connect' flag in tool-proxy cluster and reloaded instances in dc-us-east-09. Observed immediate decrease in p99 tool-proxy RPC latency to ~200ms.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed FocusDocs still seeing occasional spikes but overall improvement; collecting additional logs to validate full resolution.
2026-03-14 08:30 - Diego: Running controlled canary of v2.3.1 (patch) that changes schema fetch to async + local cache with 30s TTL. Monitoring p95/p99 for 4 hours before rollout.
mitigation: Temporary mitigation applied: disabled synchronous schema prefetch flag in tool-proxy on affected cluster (dc-us-east-09), reloaded service pool. Decreased p99 tool-proxy RPC from ~7s to ~200ms and reduced streaming timeouts. For customers still impacted we increased streaming connection idle timeout by 10s as a safety net.
next_steps:
1) Complete patch PR to make schema-fetch async with bounded parallelism and LRU cache (tool-proxy#216). 2) Add unit/integration tests that simulate slow adapter responses and assert no head-of-line blocking. 3) Roll forward v2.3.1 after successful canary and quota tests. 4) Postmortem: document root cause and add dashboard alerts for tool-proxy sync RPC increases.
Owners: Diego (Eng), Lauren (SRE), Aisha (Support)
Target ETA for fix in prod: 2026-03-16
resolution: Mitigation in-progress; full fix pending patch PR and canary validation. No permanent resolution yet.
